title: Design System: Stowaway public website (Luggage Tag)

extensions.scope: Public website only (src/features/website, src/features/legal). The signed-in app keeps its own calm-workspace system in src/styles/tokens.css, src/styles/themes.css and docs/UI_COMPONENTS.md.

motion.name: ease-tag
motion.purpose: The world's single easing for print-in, stamp and state transitions.

motion.name: print-in
motion.value: @keyframes tag-print-in { from { clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0); opacity: .2 } to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); opacity: 1 } }; 300ms to 620ms

motion.name: stamp

narrative.overview:
Every public page is one long luggage tag hung on an ocean-ink ground. The header carries the eyelet the tag hangs from, the footer closes the sheet, and everything between is printed on cool thermal stock in ink: route codes at display scale, travelers in condensed print, the plan as a routing, tickets as tear-off stubs, barcodes as the closing mark. Sections are separated by perforated tear lines with notches cut from both edges. The page reads like a trip printing itself, line by line.

The density is a printed document's: hard 2px ink strokes, dashed rules, uppercase condensed field print, and generous blocks of air between stops. Colour is almost entirely ink on stock. Coral is the one loud colour and belongs to the group's choice and the primary action; signal yellow marks what is still open. State is shown as print density (solid, half-toned, ghost), never as a new colour. Dark mode is the same tag printed in reverse.

Scope. This world governs the public website only: the landing page, How it works, Pricing, For organizers, Help, Not found and the legal pages, all inside the shared website frame and its world stylesheet (src/features/website/tag.css). The signed-in app keeps its own calm-workspace system, defined in src/styles/tokens.css and src/styles/themes.css and described in docs/UI_COMPONENTS.md and the visual identity section of docs/BRAND.md. Nothing here applies to the app, and the app's tokens are not part of this file.
keyCharacteristics: One sheet of tag stock on an ink ground, with an eyelet at the top and 22px sheet corners top and bottom.
Perforated tear lines are the section dividers; dashed rules divide inside a section.
Antonio route codes (GUA, ANT, PAN, SMR) are the display voice; Barlow carries headlines and body; Barlow Condensed prints every label and control.
Coral appears only on the group's choice and the primary action.
Print density shows state: confirmed solid, tentative half-toned, empty as a dashed ghost tag.
Motion prints in once and stamps; nothing loops.

rules.name: The Coral Ledger Rule
rules.body: Coral is spent only on the primary action, the PRIORITY stamp, the vote winner, your vote tick, the picked strip code, selection and focus. Links, hovers, the current nav item and the current strip stop are ink. If a new element wants coral, it has to be the group's choice or the one action that starts a trip.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Open Rule
rules.body: Signal yellow marks a slot or offer that is not settled yet. It never decorates, and it always carries ink text.

rules.name: The Code Is Print Rule
rules.body: Route codes are decoration of a fact already stated in words. Every code is hidden from assistive tech and the readable name sits beside it (or in screen-reader text). Barcodes are the same: decorative, always next to the text they encode.

rules.name: The Field, Not Kicker Rule
rules.body: Small uppercase print is a field on the tag: a label with its value (Travelers · 8, Paid by / Maya, Updated / October 30, 2026). It never sits alone above a heading as a section label.

rules.name: The Print Density Rule
rules.body: State is shown by how heavily something is printed. Confirmed prints solid. Tentative prints on a 5px half-tone dot with lighter weight and faded state text. Empty is a ghost: dashed rule outline, no fill, faded print ("Your idea"), or an outline-only code on the strip. Don't add a colour to show state.

rules.name: The Reverse Print Rule
rules.body: Reversal is the only inversion: dark mode prints the whole tag in reverse, and the offline stub prints in reverse (ink fill, stock text) when airplane mode is on.

dos: Do keep every public page inside the website frame so it hangs as one tag: eyelet header, stock sheet, perforated sections, footer edge.
Do separate stops and sections with the Perforation, and divide within a section with 1px or 2px dashed rule lines.
Do print state as density: solid for confirmed, the half-tone dot for tentative, a dashed ghost for empty.
Do put a readable name beside every route code and barcode, and hide the code itself from assistive tech.
Do label every demonstration honestly in fine print (example names, example votes, example amounts, real places).
Do use the Tag Head with printed fields to open a secondary page.
Do keep targets at 44px or more (segmented options, chips, checkboxes through their row label) and the coral-over-ink focus ring on everything interactive.
Do keep anything people read at 13px (0.8125rem) or larger; text-xs is remapped to it, and form fields stay at 16px.
Do pass place-category colours through categoryTone() when they colour an icon or text; dark mode lifts them toward ink.
Do keep overlays flat: no blurred shadows on dialogs, sheets, toasts or the add button; backdrops are the ground at 45%.
donts: Don't use coral outside the Coral Ledger: not for links, hovers, the current nav item, pressed chips or the lit strip stop.
Don't use signal yellow for anything that is settled.
Don't add blurred or offset drop shadows; depth is stock, stroke, holes and reverse print.
Don't put small uppercase print alone above a heading as a section label; field print always pairs a label with its value.
Don't number the stops; the routing strip identifies them by route code.
Don't retype, recolour or rotate the Stowaway wordmark or mark; use the drawn lockup from src/ui/Brand.tsx.
Don't apply this world to the signed-in app, or the app's tokens to the public site.
